config.theme: Weekly meeting of a university ecology research lab
config.author: claude-opus-5-5 (Claude Code session)

cast.theme: Weekly meeting of a university ecology research lab

personas.name: Bernard
personas.goals: Get the seagrass paper out before the renewal
personas.hidden_agenda: Wants his name last and a former student's name second

personas.name: Ama
personas.role: Postdoc who did most of the seagrass analysis
personas.goals: First authorship on the seagrass paper
personas.hidden_agenda: Needs a first-author paper for her job applications this winter

personas.name: Kieran
personas.role: PhD student, ran the freezer and the samples
personas.goals: Not be blamed for the freezer
personas.hidden_agenda: Noticed the freezer alarm was muted and didn't report it

personas.name: Sunita
personas.goals: Keep the budget and the boat schedule straight
personas.hidden_agenda: Has already told the dock the lab may cancel days

pack.title: Calloway Lab weekly meeting
pack.org: Calloway Lab, Coastal Ecology, Tidemark University (fictional)

agenda.title: The contaminated samples
agenda.goal: Decide what to do about the eelgrass samples from the freezer failure

agenda.title: Seagrass paper authorship
agenda.goal: Settle the author order before drafting

agenda.title: Boat schedule
agenda.goal: Divide the remaining boat days between projects

facts.statement: Samples contaminated in the freezer failure = 64
Boat days booked for the season = 12

beats.summary: How bad the freezer damage is; Bernard lowballs it; resequencing cost is overstated then fixed
Who goes first; a loud disagreement; a drift into the chair's retirement party
Dividing the boat days; Ama's count is off
The renewal plan; a date nobody checks

turns.speaker: Bernard
turns.text: Look, let's deal with the freezer first, because it touches everything else. Kieran, how many did we lose?

turns.speaker: Kieran
turns.text: Sorry, I've been going through the inventory all week.

turns.speaker: Bernard
turns.text: And?

turns.speaker: Kieran
turns.text: Sixty-four contaminated. Out of the two hundred and ten we collected this year.

turns.speaker: Bernard
turns.text: Sixty-four. I'd been telling people it was about thirty.

turns.speaker: Ama
turns.text: Thirty would have been bad. Sixty-four is a third of the season.

turns.speaker: Sunita
turns.text: The failure was on the third of September. Nobody caught it for two days.

turns.speaker: Bernard
turns.text: Why did nobody catch it for two days?

turns.speaker: Kieran
turns.text: The alarm— it's an old freezer.

turns.speaker: Ama
turns.text: Can we resequence them? Is the tissue still usable for that?

turns.speaker: Kieran
turns.text: For most of them. The sequencing would be about fifteen thousand.

turns.speaker: Bernard
turns.text: Fifteen thousand. Absolutely not.

turns.speaker: Ama
turns.text: Then the paper is missing a third of this year.

turns.speaker: Bernard
turns.text: We have three seasons of data. One bad batch doesn't sink a paper.

turns.speaker: Ama
turns.text: It does if the bad batch is all from the two sites the paper is about.

turns.speaker: Bernard
turns.text: Is that true?

turns.speaker: Kieran
turns.text: Mostly, yes. The north transects were all on the bottom shelf.

turns.speaker: Sunita
turns.text: I just checked the core facility quote. Resequencing is ninety-six hundred, not fifteen.

turns.speaker: Kieran
turns.text: Oh. Sorry, I had the old price with the extra library prep.

turns.speaker: Bernard
turns.text: Ninety-six hundred. Still a lot.

turns.speaker: Ama
turns.text: It's a lot less than a paper with a hole in it.

turns.speaker: Bernard
turns.text: Look. Fine. We resequence the north-transect samples only, and we pay for it out of the general account.

turns.speaker: Kieran
turns.text: I'll pull the north-transect samples and send them to the core facility on Monday.

turns.speaker: Sunita
turns.text: Somebody should really replace that freezer alarm, too.

turns.speaker: Bernard
turns.text: Look, authorship. I was thinking Ama second, and Priyanka first, since the original idea was her thesis.

turns.speaker: Ama
turns.text: Priyanka left two years ago. I did the analysis, the models, and the figures.

turns.speaker: Bernard
turns.text: The idea matters.

turns.speaker: Ama
turns.text: The idea was one paragraph in a thesis chapter. I wrote the paper.

turns.speaker: Kieran
turns.text: Can I say something?

turns.speaker: Bernard
turns.text: Go ahead.

turns.speaker: Kieran
turns.text: Sorry. I just think whoever wrote it should be first. That's the norm in this field.

turns.speaker: Bernard
turns.text: The norm in this field is that the PI decides.

turns.speaker: Kieran
turns.text: Could it maybe be co-first?

turns.speaker: Ama
turns.text: Co-first with someone who left two years ago doesn't help me.

turns.speaker: Sunita
turns.text: Did you all hear Dean Whitfield is retiring? The party is next Friday.

turns.speaker: Kieran
turns.text: Is there going to be the slideshow again? Last time it was forty minutes.

turns.speaker: Sunita
turns.text: There will absolutely be a slideshow.

turns.speaker: Ama
turns.text: Can we please finish the authorship conversation? This matters to me.

turns.speaker: Bernard
turns.text: All right. Look. Ama, you're right that you did the work.

turns.speaker: Ama
turns.text: So I'm first?

turns.speaker: Bernard
turns.text: You're first. Priyanka second, me last.

turns.speaker: Ama
turns.text: Thank you. Truly.

turns.speaker: Bernard
turns.text: And the paper goes out by December first, which means a full draft by the middle of November.

turns.speaker: Ama
turns.text: I'll have a full draft to everyone by November fifteenth.

turns.speaker: Bernard
turns.text: Fine.

turns.speaker: Sunita
turns.text: Boat time. We have twelve days booked for the rest of the season.

turns.speaker: Ama
turns.text: Twelve? I thought we had twenty. We booked extra in the spring.

turns.speaker: Sunita
turns.text: We booked twenty, and I cancelled eight when the engine was in the shop. Twelve.

turns.speaker: Bernard
turns.text: Each day is eleven-fifty, so every cancelled day is money we kept, at least.

turns.speaker: Kieran
turns.text: My transects need four days. Minimum.

turns.speaker: Ama
turns.text: The seagrass revisits need four too.

turns.speaker: Bernard
turns.text: And the new kelp pilot needs at least three.

turns.speaker: Sunita
turns.text: That's eleven. One day spare for weather.

turns.speaker: Bernard
turns.text: Then Kieran four, Ama four, kelp three, one spare.

turns.speaker: Ama
turns.text: Works for me.

turns.speaker: Sunita
turns.text: I'll update the dock calendar tonight with the split.

turns.speaker: Kieran
turns.text: Saw a seal hauled out on the dock ramp yesterday. Huge one.

turns.speaker: Ama
turns.text: The one with the scar? That's Clyde. He's been around for years.

turns.speaker: Bernard
turns.text: Renewal. The deadline is mid-February, so there's breathing room.

turns.speaker: Ama
turns.text: What are we asking for?

turns.speaker: Bernard
turns.text: Four hundred eighty thousand over three years.

turns.speaker: Sunita
turns.text: The budget justification needs the boat costs, which we now actually know.

turns.speaker: Bernard
turns.text: We could ask for more, given costs went up. I'd want to see the numbers first.

turns.speaker: Kieran
turns.text: Will the freezer thing hurt the renewal?

turns.speaker: Bernard
turns.text: Not if the resequenced data is in the preliminary results.

turns.speaker: Ama
turns.text: That's another reason the paper has to go out on time.

turns.speaker: Bernard
turns.text: Sunita, could you start the budget spreadsheet for the renewal this week?

turns.speaker: Sunita
turns.text: Yes. I'll have a first version by Friday.

turns.speaker: Kieran
turns.text: Who's writing the data management plan? Last time it was a mess.

turns.speaker: Bernard
turns.text: Look, I think that's enough for today. Good meeting. Mostly.

turns.speaker: Ama
turns.text: Mostly.
